scope: Pure symmetric12-qubit states with full partition(2,2,2,2,1,1,1,1).

C3.orbitCounting: Four doubled points require one three-point orbit plus one polar double point. Four simple points require one three-point orbit plus the other polar simple point. The resulting Dicke support is one of the two listed sets.
C3.contradiction: Uniform moments through order3 force a negative probability.

C4.orbitCounting: Both the doubled set and the simple set must be single four-point orbits; no polar point is possible. Thus P(z)=(z^4-u)^2(z^4-v), with u,v nonzero and distinct.
C4.doubleRootCubicLemma: For (w-u)^2(w-v), |u²v|=1 and equal magnitudes of the two middle coefficients imply each squared magnitude is at most9+6sqrt(3).
C4.lemmaDerivation: Rotate u to r>0 and write v=r^-2 exp(i phi). Equal magnitudes factor as (r²-1)[r6-3r4-3r2+1+4r3cos(phi)]=0. If r=1 the magnitude is at most3. Otherwise h=r+1/r>=2 obeys cos(phi)=h(6-h²)/4, hence h<=1+sqrt3, and the squared middle magnitude is3(h²-1)<=9+6sqrt3<25.
C4.contradiction: The required magnitude33 exceeds the universal bound, which is less than5.

ordersAtLeast5.argument: A nonaxial orbit under an order-m proper rotation has exactlym points. With onlyfour doubled points and at mosttwo axial points, m>=5 is impossible.

groupClassificationReason: Finite subgroups of SO(3) are cyclic, dihedral or polyhedral. If no element has order>=3, only C1,C2,D2 remain. Continuous rotation symmetry is impossible for eight distinct points.
limitation: The target partition remains unsettled for general geometries in the three remaining proper-group classes. No numerical failure is used as a global exclusion.
